categories.name: Technical SEO
what_works: robots.txt is clean, current, and correctly points to the sitemap
HTTP→HTTPS and www→non-www redirects are clean single-hop 301s
Homepage title, meta description, canonical, viewport and hreflang tags are all present and server-rendered
Sitemap structure exactly matches the live URL set — no orphan pages
TLS certificate valid and auto-renewed via Shopify

findings.title: Site returns HTTP 429 on theme-rendered pages under concurrent load
findings.evidence: Repeated requests to /, /products/canvas, /collections/frontpage and /pages/contact returned HTTP 429 with retry-after:60 for 10+ minutes, while static assets (robots.txt, sitemap.xml) stayed at 200 throughout.
findings.recommendation: Check installed Shopify apps for an overly aggressive bot/rate-limit configuration on storefront rendering, and check Search Console Crawl Stats for real-world 429 spikes during traffic surges.

findings.title: hreflang for /hi and /ru is structurally correct, but translated content depth is unverified
findings.evidence: Homepage correctly declares hreflang for en/hi/ru/x-default, matching parallel /hi/ and /ru/ sitemaps with the same 6 products and 5 pages.
findings.recommendation: Confirm /hi and /ru render genuinely translated copy, not English text under a translated URL — hreflang pointing at un-translated pages provides no real value to those searchers.

findings.title: Homepage meta description exceeds recommended length
findings.evidence: Meta description is ~255 characters; Google typically truncates snippets around 155–160.
findings.recommendation: Trim to ~150–160 characters, front-loading “award-winning Indian artist in London, limited edition prints.”

findings.title: Security headers: solid baseline but minimal CSP and no Referrer-Policy
findings.evidence: HSTS, X-Frame-Options and X-Content-Type-Options are all present; CSP only restricts frame-ancestors/mixed-content (no script-src); no Referrer-Policy header observed; HSTS max-age is ~91 days, below the 1-year threshold for preload eligibility.
findings.recommendation: Largely Shopify-platform-controlled and low risk for this site — low priority.

categories.name: Content Quality
what_works: Brand naming (“Inquisitive Arts” / “Anugrah Mishra”) is consistent across titles, meta, schema and copy
Dedicated About / Artists / Portfolio / Contact pages give the right structural foundation for E-E-A-T content
Clean H1/title alignment and fully populated Open Graph tags on product pages

findings.title: Product descriptions are thin, generic print-on-demand copy
findings.evidence: ~99 words per product; “Looking to add a little flair to your room or office? Look no further—this canvas has a vivid, fade-resistant print…” is stock POD marketing copy with no dimensions, technique detail, or story behind the piece.
findings.recommendation: Write unique 300–500 word descriptions per artwork: the story/inspiration, medium and process, precise dimensions, and a note in the artist's own voice. Highest-leverage content fix on the whole site.

findings.title: Real artist credentials are absent from the pages meant to convert on them
findings.evidence: Anugrah Mishra is a real awarded artist (Freelands Painting Prize 2024, Anglia Ruskin Creative Showcase, Saatchi Art, MutualArt) — none of this appears on product pages, which read as generic stock listings instead.
findings.recommendation: Add a short “about the artist” block on every product page referencing real exhibition history and the award — this is close to a free trust/conversion win.

findings.title: No blog or story-driven content surface
findings.evidence: /blog and /blogs both return 404; no editorial content endpoint exists anywhere on the site.
findings.recommendation: Stand up a blog for inspiration stories, process posts, and collection launches — a natural fit for a gallery, and currently a total content-strategy gap.

findings.title: Unfilled placeholder address live in legally-required product text
findings.evidence: Every product's GPSR compliance text reads: “You can also write to us at 123 Main Street, Anytown, Country…” — an unedited template placeholder, visible to every shopper.
findings.recommendation: Replace with the real registered business address immediately — cheap fix, outsized trust impact for a compliance-relevant statement.

findings.title: About/Artists/Portfolio page depth could not be directly confirmed
findings.evidence: Pages exist in navigation and sitemap, but rate-limiting blocked direct retrieval of body copy this session; the one fully-verified page (a product) uses generic templated copy, which raises the risk these pages follow the same pattern.
findings.recommendation: Directly review these pages for a specific bio (training, exhibitions, UK location) and at least one first-person photo — downgrade this finding to Info if they're already substantive.

categories.name: On-Page & E-commerce SEO
what_works: Product structured data includes correct price, currency (GBP) and availability — many small Shopify stores omit this entirely
Canonical tags are correctly self-referencing with no variant-URL duplication risk
Collection and product-grid image alt text follows a consistent, descriptive “Title – Artist Name” pattern

findings.title: Catalog depth is critically thin for competitive e-commerce SEO
findings.evidence: 6 product URLs across 2 collections, roughly 4 distinct artworks priced £40–£44, no size/subject/room filtering.
findings.recommendation: Either treat the site as a portfolio/brand-search destination and stop chasing commercial category keywords, or commit to meaningfully expanding the catalog before investing further in product-page SEO.

findings.title: Zero reviews or social proof anywhere on the site
findings.evidence: No aggregateRating, no rendered reviews — theme loads component-rating.css but no rating data exists to populate it.
findings.recommendation: Install a reviews app and actively request reviews post-purchase; for a £40+ purchase from an unfamiliar brand this is one of the highest-leverage trust signals available.

findings.title: No delivery, returns, or trust signals near Add to Cart
findings.evidence: Buy box shows only Add to Cart and Shop Pay; refund policy link exists only in the footer; no dedicated shipping-policy page exists at all.
findings.recommendation: Add a short trust strip beside the CTA: delivery window, return window, secure-checkout mention — standard on every competing UK print retailer.

findings.title: Product URL slugs are non-descriptive
findings.evidence: On-page title is descriptive (“Landscape II– Anugrah Mishra”) but the URL is /products/canvas-5.
findings.recommendation: Rename slugs to e.g. /products/landscape-ii-canvas-print-anugrah-mishra — Shopify auto-redirects on handle change, so this is low-risk.

findings.title: No breadcrumbs or related-products module
findings.evidence: No Home > Collection > Product breadcrumb trail and no “you may also like” section anywhere in the product page DOM.
findings.recommendation: Add breadcrumbs (cheap win, also unlocks BreadcrumbList schema) and a simple cross-sell block.

findings.title: Product meta description far exceeds display length
findings.evidence: 320 characters on the product page checked, roughly double Google's ~155–160 char display limit, with no price or CTA included.
findings.recommendation: Trim to ~150 characters leading with product name and price, e.g. “Landscape II canvas print by Anugrah Mishra — from £40, ships UK-wide.”

categories.name: Structured Data
what_works: Valid WebSite + SearchAction schema, correctly formed for sitelinks search box eligibility
Product schema's Offer block has correct numeric price, ISO currency and availability enum

findings.title: Duplicate Organization schema, and one copy is a broken unfilled template
findings.evidence: Homepage <head> emits two Organization blocks. The first is hand-coded with logo set to the literal placeholder “path-to-your-logo.png” (unresolvable). The second, theme-generated block is correct.
findings.recommendation: Delete the hand-coded block entirely — it's redundant and its broken logo field is actively harmful to entity-clarity signals.

findings.title: Product schema is missing reviews, return policy and shipping details
findings.evidence: aggregateRating/review, hasMerchantReturnPolicy and shippingDetails are all absent from Product JSON-LD, despite a refund-policy page existing on-site.
findings.recommendation: Add hasMerchantReturnPolicy and shippingDetails to the schema, stand up a real shipping-policy page, and start collecting reviews so aggregateRating can populate.

findings.title: sameAs array is mostly empty and includes Shopify's own default TikTok, not the store's
findings.evidence: sameAs holds 6 empty strings, a correct Instagram link, and “https://tiktok.com/@shopify” — a leftover default value.
findings.recommendation: Fill in the store's real social profiles and remove the erroneous Shopify TikTok entry — it currently misattributes this small gallery's entity to Shopify's own account.

categories.name: Performance
what_works: Shopify CDN responsive images are correctly implemented with full srcset breakpoints everywhere
Automatic WebP delivery confirmed live: a 4.5MB source JPEG was served to a real browser as a 67KB WebP
Native lazy-loading used correctly — below-fold images lazy, hero loads eagerly
HTML responses are Brotli-compressed with long-lived cache headers on static assets

findings.title: Severe third-party script bloat — 165+ requests on a single homepage load
findings.evidence: Two separate Google tag containers, DoubleClick and Merchant Center pixels, 4 sandboxed Shopify web-pixel workers, PushOwl, Sendvio, a Shopify Forms app, and an orphaned jQuery 1.10.1 loaded from ajax.googleapis.com — plus the full checkout-web bundle preloading on the homepage itself.
findings.recommendation: Audit installed apps and remove or defer anything not actively driving revenue; each pixel competes for main-thread time and directly hurts INP.

findings.title: Unused Google Fonts request loads 26 unrelated font families
findings.evidence: Homepage requests fonts.googleapis.com with 26 families (Aclonica, Shrikhand, Permanent Marker, etc.) — none match the theme, which actually self-hosts Newsreader and Halant.
findings.recommendation: Find and remove the source (likely a leftover app/page-builder font-picker) — pure wasted DNS/connection/CSS weight.

findings.title: Large hero image likely driving LCP
findings.evidence: Homepage hero JPEG fallback is ~547KB at 1800px width — the largest single asset on the page and the probable LCP candidate.
findings.recommendation: Re-export the hero source at tighter compression; a modern re-encode of a photographic hero at this size should land closer to 150–250KB.

findings.title: Full checkout bundle preloads on the homepage, not just at checkout
findings.evidence: 10+ checkout-web files plus ~20 Shop Pay accelerated-checkout chunks load on first homepage visit.
findings.recommendation: Largely platform-controlled (Shop Pay integration) — the real lever is reducing everything else competing for the same budget.

categories.name: AI Search Readiness (GEO)
what_works: UCP/agentic-commerce infrastructure (checkout, cart, catalog search) is fully live with real merchant/payment IDs, not placeholders
robots.txt is clean and permissive for every major AI crawler — GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended all fall under an open wildcard allow
Brand entity naming is consistent across meta, schema and copy

findings.title: Product copy is too generic and short to be a citable AI-search passage
findings.evidence: The ~99-word product description is generic marketing language, well under the ~134–167 word self-contained, fact-dense passage AI answer engines tend to extract and cite.
findings.recommendation: Front-load a specific, quotable 1–2 sentence factual summary (medium, size, technique, story) before the marketing language — shared fix with the Content Quality product-copy finding.

findings.title: Broken Organization schema undermines entity-clarity for AI systems
findings.evidence: Same broken placeholder logo and stray Shopify TikTok link in sameAs (see Structured Data) directly weaken the brand/authority signals GEO frameworks weight most after content quality.
findings.recommendation: Same fix as the Structured Data findings — resolves both issues at once.

findings.title: No blog is a structural GEO gap, not just a content gap
findings.evidence: No live blog endpoint exists; AI citation research shows recent, first-person, self-contained passages are disproportionately what gets cited, and a product-only site has no surface for that.
findings.recommendation: Same underlying fix as the Content Quality blog finding — the highest-leverage new-content investment available for AI-citation eligibility.

findings.title: llms.txt exists but is generic Shopify boilerplate, not brand-specific content
findings.evidence: llms.txt is byte-for-byte identical to /agents.md — platform infrastructure docs with no curated facts about the artist or brand. Google explicitly ignores llms.txt for Search/AI Overviews, so this has no Google-side citation value regardless.
findings.recommendation: Low priority — real content on the pages themselves matters far more than this file. If keeping it, replace the boilerplate with a short curated brand summary for non-Google AI crawlers that do read it.

categories.name: Images
what_works: Collection and product-listing images use strong, consistent, artwork-specific alt text (“Title – Artist Name”)
Every content image ships a full responsive srcset via the Shopify CDN
Explicit width/height attributes on all real content images keep CLS risk low

findings.title: Hero and banner images have no alt text
findings.evidence: 3 of 17 homepage images have alt="" — including the full-bleed hero (“Refugee's Resilience and Dreams”) and two other large content banners.
findings.recommendation: Add descriptive alt text to every content image, following the naming convention already used correctly on collection pages.

findings.title: Generic, duplicated alt text on product thumbnails
findings.evidence: Size/frame mockup thumbnails on product pages all share the identical alt text “Product mockup” regardless of which size is shown.
findings.recommendation: Differentiate alt text per thumbnail (e.g. “16×16 inch room mockup”) — low priority, secondary images.

phases.name: Phase 1 — Critical fixes
items: Replace the placeholder address (“123 Main Street, Anytown, Country”) in GPSR compliance text with the real registered address
Delete the broken hand-coded Organization schema block (dead logo URL) and clean the sameAs array (remove Shopify's TikTok, add real profiles)
Decide the site's identity deliberately: artist portfolio or commerce-led store — and align the homepage title/meta accordingly
Add alt text to the homepage hero and other missing banner images

phases.name: Phase 2 — High-impact improvements
items: Rewrite all 6 product descriptions: real dimensions, technique, story, artist credentials (Freelands Painting Prize 2024)
Install a reviews app and begin collecting post-purchase reviews
Add hasMerchantReturnPolicy + shippingDetails to product schema and stand up a real shipping-policy page
Audit installed Shopify apps and remove/defer unused trackers (PushOwl, Sendvio, orphaned jQuery, unused Google Fonts request)
Add a delivery/returns trust strip next to Add to Cart

phases.name: Phase 3 — Content & authority
items: Launch a blog: inspiration stories, process posts, exhibition/collection launches
Add an “about the artist” block to every product page referencing real exhibitions and the award
Rename product URL slugs to descriptive, keyword-relevant handles
Add breadcrumbs and a related-products module
Confirm /hi and /ru serve genuinely translated content

phases.name: Phase 4 — Monitoring
items: Watch Search Console Crawl Stats for real-world 429s during traffic spikes
Track branded vs. non-branded query performance — branded search is currently the site's only proven strength
Re-run this audit after Phase 1–2 fixes to confirm score improvement
